description: Persisted supervised-sitting registry, the one liveness probe (kill+start-time), the four write moments, and the boot re-adopt pass that runs before any ending stamp

The ONE evidence-to-ending path: a done/incomplete checkout stands and is reaped, a death with no checkout is stamped failed with a mandatory reason class, and confirm-and-reap frees the process for every seat
JSON CLI over the registry and the death stamp for non-node callers: --op NAME [--registry PATH] [--db PATH] [--payload JSON|PATH|-]

The explicit door list [T4-R7]: every launch path is wrapped (supervisor spawn writes the registry row) or marked unsupervised, plus the E_GOAL_NOT_LIVE refusal that spawns, stamps and enqueues nothing

The one liveness answer for a (goal, seat) sitting - supervised/alive/unknown off the registry, replacing the tmux pane, the cgroup carrier and tick silence [T4-R8]; also a JSON main for team-kit's python
The ONE owed-work computer [T4-R7, C-15]: deriveOwed answers class A (non-terminal ending), class B (unread mail) and class R (graph-derived launchability [T1-R3]) from one call, and never enqueues

The wrapped spawn door's admit checks (hold, cage admit, lane reach, boot prompt, store disagree) and the ONE heartStore.enqueue on the owed path - the launches seeding and reconcile used to make independently

The ONE read api for the eight recovery numbers in {workspace}/.rbtv/config/ignite/recovery.json [spec-recovery 2.1]: strict schema validation (all keys required, integers only, extra keys refused, 0/negative refused), configuration-error with NO in-code fallback, plus copy-if-absent seeding from the packaged seed
The packaged seed of the recovery config file - the spec table defaults, copied to the instance path iff absent and never overwritten by an upgrade

The per-kind progress-signal collectors [T4-R1, CF-2]: the closed table of what advances the ONE supervisor-owned last_progress_at (file-writing, chat-only, planning/orchestrator, judge) and what explicitly does not

The no-progress kill decision off last_progress_at alone, and the CLOSED list of three pause conditions [T1-R19, D-1-ruling]: a verified open ask, an open provider-backoff window, a disarmed incomplete lane until its named event

The operational checkpoint contract [D4, T1-R2, T4-R2]: the three-field progress note, the tab-separated side-effect journal written BEFORE each external act with a relaunch skip on the idempotency key, and the relaunch prompt (brief + note + the verbatim continue-instruction)

The attempt counter that replaced both byte-equality brakes [spec-recovery 5, T4-R3]: counts a same-reason retry per (driver, subject, reason class), refuses a volatile key, resets ONLY on the four named re-arm events, and REFUSES the designed hourly frozen repeat [C-5]

The exit at N [T1-R8, D-2-ruling]: stamps the lane disarmed incomplete through the ending api and writes ONE signature-grouped ask RECORD per failure signature (never per lane, never a Slack write), plus the resume act that consumes the disarmed flag

The recovery relaunch budget [T1-R6, C-11]: both caps off the ending row counters, ask-resume refused at the spend door, the one bounded D6 leader handoff payload [T4-R6] with the ask text the leader reads, the leader-instruction inbox and its drain, and the daemon act that executes each of the four leader instructions [CF-3, D6]

The ONE reader of the two owner-editable recognition lists [spec-recovery 3]: case-insensitive substring match, first list wins, both-hit and unrecognised both fall to CONFIGURATION (fail closed), plus the content fingerprint a list edit changes (a config-change re-arm)
The versioned TRANSIENT recognition list - quota / rate-limit / provider-down class tokens and their common strings. Owner-editable data; an edit is a config-change named re-arm
The versioned CONFIGURATION recognition list - model-not-found / bad slug / auth-rejected class tokens and their common strings. Owner-editable data; an edit is a config-change named re-arm

What each provider class does to a lane [spec-recovery 3, C-5, C-10]: transient never strikes and takes ONE recorded pass through the shared table's alternates then backs off on loader-supplied numbers with the kill clock paused; configuration is an ordinary failed + strike; a per-seat model override suppresses reroute; and the readable provider_backoff_until / provider_backoff_waiting / reroute_pending facts impl-alarms consumes

The daemon's read of the SHARED routing table models.csv - the same file cast route reads, so a reroute can never name a model cast cannot launch. Eligible alternates are mode=cli use=route rows minus the lane's own pin and anything already tried this attempt

The shared routing table [spec-recovery 3]: the owner-editable routing axes (level, scores, cost, web, image) for every launchable model. Two readers - cast route's verdict and the daemon's provider-lane reroute

The per-goal reconcile pass: the ledger classifier, the provider-lane reroute, the per-lane skip that unfreezes siblings, the fail-closed leader-chair resolution, and the relaunch-budget handoff to the leader plus the drain of its answer (moved from engine/ by spec-component-map §2)

The once-a-cadence walk over every daemon-assigned goal: lane reads, pause truth, seeding, the loud named skip of a daemon goal with no taskforce, and the observation facts the frozen driver consumes (moved from engine/)
Seeds a goal folder taskforce into the store and enqueues what is due, skipping whatever the goal execution record says is finished (moved from engine/)
The shared per-goal execution record: the session join both lanes publish to, and the owner-ask open set behind it (moved from engine/)
The ending-store READERS the recovery path uses: done set, owner-hold set and launchability, bound to the workspace store the goal folder resolves to (moved from engine/)
classifyEnding over ending+armed - the classifier the one owed-work computer reads (moved from engine/)
The spawn/fire path: launch-spec resolution per seat, the cage composition seam, carriers, tmux seats and the orphan rescan (moved from server/spawn/)
The shared launch-spec resolver every spawn goes through - catalog, host reads, preflight and the effort ladder interpreter (moved from launch-profiles/)
The worker harness session settings the spawn path materializes into a caged seat folder (moved from config/)

Act on a seat you are not sitting in — rule on its ended session (`instruct`), accept its finished work (`accept`), close or relaunch it, or route a FAIL back to its receiver. The leader-facing reference for the `supervise` door

The supervision CLI — the daemon's and a leader's remedial surface over a run: the launch composer, the readiness arithmetic and the acts that repair a seat. The other half of the `coordinate` entry point, split by audience (owner ruling 2026-08-25); seat-facing coordination stays there

Process truth: ps snapshot, process identity, the live-process and live-harness predicates, exit verification and the pid reaper — registry probe input, never a second liveness surface (spec-component-map §3)

The daemon-executes-mechanical-remedies home: the lifecycle-inflight marker, the hidden `lifecycle-exec` verb, the bus alarm, the caller-side fork and the disposition sequences (spec-component-map §3)
The ready-seat arithmetic, the derived `dead` state and the launch-admission predicate — the verdict computer the owed-work unification reads instead of forking a second one (spec-component-map §3)
The lane-aware launch composer: seat discovery, descriptor validation, the boot prompt, harness command resolution and session-open (spec-component-map §3)
The attest-exit arm and the session closer — the one death stamp the independent stampers were replaced by (spec-component-map §3)
The asserted-identity launch bound: the paneless cgroup predicate that corroborates a `--as` claim, folded into the registry rather than kept as a second liveness answer (spec-component-map §3)
